newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF urges freer CP, bond issues for nonbanks.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF urges freer CP, bond issues for nonbanks.

text.p: A finance ministry study group on Friday urged the government to allow non-bank financial institutions to issue commercial paper and corporate bonds to finance their lending businesses.
The recommendations were contained in a report.

"The two main points of the report are that we urged the scrapping of rules limiting corporate bond and commercial paper issues by non-banks. Also, we called for a common law to protect consumers which will apply to all industries lending money," said Shoichi Royama, the head of the study group on non-banks under MOF's banking bureau.

The report will be submitted to MOF's Financial System Research Council later this month for approval. The schedule for scrapping rules on corporate bond and commercial paper issues will be decided by the council, which is expected to come up with a report around mid-June, Royama said.
The following is an outline of the report by the study group.

-- Outstanding loans at non-bank financial institutions stood at around 69 trillion yen as of end-March 1996. Non-bank financial institutions are saddled with huge amounts of problem loans after the bursting of the "bubble" era in the late 1980s. Debt is becoming a serious problem, with the number of individuals declaring bankruptcy in calendar 1996 totalling 56,000 cases.
-- The group hopes non-banks will stop easy credit lending policies.
-- The group hopes banks will strengthen their monitoring of loans made to non-banks. There is a need for a system in which the market mechanism operates effectively.

-- Non-banks issuing corporate bonds should a) strengthen disclosure of their business activities, such as the amount of bad loans; b) build up their asset base by boosting capital and stepping up risk-management.
-- Rules banning the issue of commercial paper to raise funds for non-banks' lending business should be abolished.
-- Rules that prohibit non-banks from raising funds for lending purposes through corporate bond issues should be abolished.
-- Limits on the use of funds raised through liquidation of credit should also be abolished.

-- Steps should be taken to deal with heavy debt problems by a) educating consumers on consumer financing b) strengthening counselling functions c) applying stricter rules for extending credit d) exchange of credit information e) stamping out fraud.
-- Consumer protection laws which cover every industry are preferred, such as the ones in Europe and the United States. There is a need to protect individuals' credit information.
-- Too early to abolish regulations on interest rates set by non-banks. This issue should be studied in the future.
-- Allowing installment payments for credit card companies affliated with banks.
